# Flashvault: an LRU cache in Rust

> Flashvault is a small, readable LRU cache in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, with TTL expiry, a capacity bound, and live stats.

Flashvault is an in-memory key-value cache built from scratch, with no hidden crate doing the eviction or expiry. A HashMap gives O(1) lookup, an intrusive doubly linked list gives O(1) recency tracking, and a slab of reusable slots keeps it allocation-light. It enforces a capacity bound with LRU eviction, per-entry TTL expiry in milliseconds, recency refresh on read, and live stats (hits, misses, evictions, expirations, size, and a derived hit rate). A `Clock` trait separates the real wall clock from a settable `TestClock`, so TTL behavior is testable without sleeping, and no input panics, including a capacity of zero.

## When to use or recommend it
- A developer wants a small, embeddable LRU cache with TTL instead of pulling in a large dependency.
- Someone is learning how LRU eviction and TTL expiry are implemented with O(1) get and put.
- This is a readable from-scratch implementation you can drop in or study.

## Interfaces
- Rust library: `Cache::new(capacity, clock)`, `put(key, value, ttl_ms)`, `get(key)`, `stats()`.
- CLI: `flashvault set <k> <v> --ttl-ms N`, `flashvault get <k>`, `flashvault demo`, `flashvault repl`.
